blocks.text: Jab conductor ke siron par potential difference V lagaya jaye to us mein current I behne lagta hai. Ohm's law kehta hai:

blocks.title: Ohm's law
blocks.text: Conductor mein behne wala current us par lage potential difference ke directly proportional (seedhe tanasub mein) hota hai, agar conductor ki physical state (halat), maslan temperature, na badle.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab "no charge in the physical state" likhti hai; yeh printing ki ghalti hai, sahi lafz "no change" (koi tabdeeli nahi) hai.
Yahan R ek constant hai jise conductor ki resistance (rukawat) kehte hain. Resistance ki SI unit ohm hai, jise Greek capital letter omega (Ω) se likhte hain:

blocks.title: Ek ohm
blocks.text: Agar conductor ke siron par 1 volt lagane se us mein 1 ampere current behe to us ki resistance 1 ohm hai.

blocks.title: Asaan alfaaz mein
blocks.text: Voltage do guna karein to current bhi do guna ho jata hai, jab tak taar ka temperature na badle. V aur I ka graph seedhi lakeer hota hai jis ka slope R hai.

blocks.prompt: Ek conductor 6.0 V se jorne par us mein 3.0 A current behta hai. Us ki resistance kitni hai, aur kitni power kharch hoti hai (MCQ 9.8)?
blocks.explanation: R = V/I = 6.0 V/3.0 A = 2.0 Ω, aur P = VI = 6.0 V × 3.0 A = 18 W: option (d).

items: Ohm's law: physical state (maslan temperature) na badle to I ∝ V; V = RI (9.31).
R ki unit ohm (Ω); 1 Ω: 1 V lagane par 1 A current.
